project.name: Cellerator

tasks.title: Specify relation calculus and explicit arithmetic profiles
tasks.mechanism: Extend the canonical relation semantics with a small calculus descriptor, not a generic graph. Specify scalar support VJP, orientation and cotangent axes, overwrite gradient output, f32 accumulation, and two explicit contraction profiles: f32 operands, or f32 operands rounded once to binary16 nearest-even before either sparse or WMMA multiplication. Retain N1 public semantics. An update is a separately ordered effect with old/new generation bindings; a compiler or candidate identity is not mathematical equivalence.
acceptance: Native and compiler-origin descriptors compare every mathematical field while excluding runtime bindings/provenance.
Scalar contraction split-K sums partials; no edge-channel concatenation or implicit normalization is introduced.
Mixed-profile semantics and straight-line real-valued VJP versus storage rounding are explicitly distinguished.
tests: Same extents/different biological axes; orientation reversal; profile mismatch; unknown effect kind; edge-channel rejection.
tasks.principal_risk: An f16 provider must never silently round operands requested as full f32.

Public declaration sketch and demo agree; no declaration is installed without real implementation.

Small updates, ties-to-even, signed zeros and overflow behavior are tested against the stated rounding policy.

tasks.title: Connect updates to readiness and generation publication
tasks.mechanism: Integrate the runtime readiness component, sparse/hybrid gradient dispatch and updates into the pair. Owner stream performs old-generation work, waits for registered reader completion, updates values, then records publication. A successful metadata transition means publication enqueued; completion is checked through event/stream observation. Initial publish and external replacement obey the same reader discipline. No cudaDeviceSynchronize or per-step allocation.
acceptance: Publication happens after all writes; newly published generation is consumed on another nonblocking stream.
Owner can update after reader-return enqueues completion without host-wide synchronization.
No false generation advancement or successful-receipt emission after rejected/failed enqueue.
tests: Two update styles across at least three generations; delayed reader; immediate next forward; stale-generation rejection.
tasks.principal_risk: Reusing an event does not preserve the previous generation storage contents.

tasks.title: Add bounded consumer read leases and writer join
tasks.mechanism: Implement one outstanding const value-read lease for v1, recyclable after end_read records consumer completion and submits owner-stream wait. This small bound permits sequential consumers on arbitrary same-device streams without adding concurrent prepared execution. The next writer rejects an unreturned lease rather than blocking the host indefinitely. Tickets carry identity, generation and nonce; duplicate return, wrong stream and old token replay fail. Do not reuse an event until its relevant waits have been submitted in the serialized protocol.
acceptance: Producer-ready and consumer-done edges are both explicit and tested without host/device-global sync.
A stale lease cannot release a newer reader; next mutation joins the correct completion event.
Pool exhaustion is explicit; the one-lease limit is documented as a bounded runtime policy, not mathematics.
tests: Delayed D2D reader; begin/begin rejection; stale return; return then immediate update; repeat on two distinct consumer streams.
tasks.principal_risk: Allowing unrestricted concurrent borrowing would require a larger reclamation design outside this epic.
